key_insight: Twisting multilayer MoS2 moiré stacks breaks symmetry and can strongly tune and activate shift-current photocurrent components for solar-light harvesting.
engineering_relevance: This suggests twist angle can be used as a design knob to engineer new in-plane nonlinear photovoltaic responses in layered TMD devices.
method: Built a Slater-Koster tight-binding model for large moiré supercells, parametrized from first-principles.
Compared the model against density functional theory and Wannier-interpolated calculations.
Analyzed shift-current conductivity and shift distance across mono-, bi-, and trilayer and twisted bilayer/trilayer systems.
evidence_signal: The tight-binding model reproduces band-edge electronic structure and the main spectral features of the shift-current conductivity, matching DFT and Wannier results.
watch_item: Accuracy is strongest near the band edges, so predictions for higher-energy features or very different twist configurations may require further first-principles validation.
paper_title: Twistronic control of shift current in multilayer moiré system
